I just love India with its myriad cultures & traditions and nowhere is it as obvious when it comes to child care practices.
Whether it is the big kala tikka of kajal in Maharashtra to ‘daak naam’ and ‘bhalo naam’ in Bengal to the gold infused water in the South to the ghee massage in the North; each state with its own unique style.
6th June is celebrated as complementary feeding day in India. There  is a reason…it is the 6th day of the 6th month of the year…so it is a reminder to start complementary foods when the child completes 6 months of age.
But what do we mean by complementary foods?
As the word suggests, complementary means something which completes, enhances or adds what is lacking to make something perfect.
Till 6 months of age, breast feeding provides complete and the best nutrition for a child’s physical and mental needs.
But after 6 months, the child’s needs increase such that need something in ‘addition’ to breast milk.
That something is complementary feeds. It is in no way supposed to completely replace breast feeding. In fact, breast feeding is to be continued till 2 years and beyond ALONG WITH  complementary foods. 
So, the 1st  step is to understand that complementary feeding is not a replacement feeding, rather it is a supportive feeding for breast milk to provide complete nutrition to a child as per its growing needs.
There are multiple fallacies like the ‘when’, ‘how’ , ‘what’ regarding complementary foods.
Today we tackled the first ’when’.
Stay tuned!

“Chauka, chauka!” 
I just attended the cricket premier league held in my building. The sheer energy around the event was mind boggling! Whether it was a girl bowling with aplomb to her own twin in the opposing team …or the motivating speech by captains… or some players flinging their caps down in angst about a dropped catch à la our national cricketers… it was a spectacle worth watching.
Tiny tots explaining the nuances of league cricket to me with such authority…tiny girls who are so soft spoken when they come to the clinic for a checkup, suddenly screaming their lungs out when their team-mate gets a wicket…a captain taking the catch of the opposing captain, notwithstanding the fact that they are best friends…
Whether it was the commentator who kept coming up with newer superlatives & witticisms to describe every delivery…or the organizers who thought of funky T shirts, adding a swag to every team…or the audience who kept confusing the score keeper…cricket has a way of pulling everyone around it in its vortex…
As a team owner, I understood first hand that you feel such a sense of responsibility. Suddenly, the only thing you want is for your team to win the trophy…
Sports bring out the best in human beings…a teenager who has just moved up the cricketing echelons, gave a fantastic display of sportsman spirit, by ensuring that an inadvertent injustice to the opposing team was averted while explaining his own fault to the umpire…twas enough to bring out the goosebumps indeed!!!

“Hey mom, is this your diaper?” Most little girls find a sanitary napkin when exploring their mom’s cupboard.
Most are embarrassed & use the age-old method to brush the query off by saying,” You are too young for this” or “Do not ask unnecessary questions.” This is because parents are unprepared to answer.
So how to answer if such questions pop out of the blue. E.g., “I’m a little busy right now, can we speak about this later.” Or “You will find it difficult to understand right now, just like ‘trigonometry’, but can we speak about this after your nth birthday.” Or “It’s a part of becoming an adult, I will explain it at the right age.”
So, keep the communication lines open. If make the topic a taboo, it becomes ‘forbidden fruit’, always more attractive compared to the routine fare. So, it’s better to keep a normal bodily activity mundane.
Remember, each conversation with your child should open the doors to the next one. The doors should never be shut so hard that they cannot be reopened. Children appreciate honesty, they understand that some things can’t be understood or explained right now; but they like to know that they can ask their parents anything, without being yelled at for their candor.
So, the next time your little one stumps you with a question, take a deep breath, pause & just say with a smile, “Can I answer in some time?” Think of an age-appropriate answer & don’t forget to answer in some time! 
Coz, the hand which rocks the cradle can best help her little one!

“Hey mom, by the way I started my periods today.”
However much we crib about the gen Alphas, they are like rockstars in the way they manage their menses.
In fact, they are so casual about it that they take stains, sanitary napkin mishaps in their stride.
They know tissue paper hacks in case of napkin non availability, warm compresses relieve pain & that one should keep a period diary.
A major reason for this nonchalance is that they have prior knowledge.
They also have a unique perspective on things.
A teen once explained menstruation to me: -
“Sooo, the uterus it has one job okhay, to host a baby. Every month it becomes nice & soft for the baby. But if there is no baby, the uterus throws a tantrum & destroys its own lining & the egg. This shedding is called menstruation.” (sic)
Physiology lesson 101 indeed!
Earlier, menstruation was considered a taboo topic, something to be embarrassed about, something to be hidden, something for others to stay away from.
But now schools hold detailed sessions to educate children, in fact there is a separate chapter on the reproductive system, where children of both genders are taught the basics of human anatomy & physiology.
One thing is clear that in the era of the internet, children can get hold of any information they please at their fingertips. Sometimes, it can be age-inappropriate. It’s always better to get the information from books, parents, teachers or doctors. 
In our next blog let us see how to deal with these questions.

Happy birthday to youuuuuu…
Some birthdays are more special than others.
It was a busy morning when the last patient entered without any obvious complaints…the parents said they just came to see me.
After checking the naughty cherub who just wanted to grab & throw all the toys, I turned & voila, there was a birthday cake on my table.
Their little one had turned one.
The mother thanked me with tear filled eyes.
It took me back to the same day last year when I was resuscitating the same child.
There are moments in a doctor’s life which take years off your life.
Moments when you have to tell expectant parents that their much-awaited child may not make it.
Or even if they make it, the brain may have suffered irreversible damage due to lack of oxygen.
It’s the stuff of nightmares for the parents as well as the doctor, especially with the internet prognosticating doomsday!
Every milestone is scrutinised instead of enjoyed!
But sometimes, life sends you a miracle, which gives you the fortitude to continue your journey.
The moment you hear a heartbeat, just when you about to give up, the exhilaration when you hear the baby give a robust cry.
For a paediatrician, its the sweetest sound in the world, competing with a toddler’s gurgle for the first place. 
They say ‘Faith can move mountains.’
Whether you call it God, faith of parents, will of the child or the determined skill of a doctor, there are some baby’s who defy all odds.
And they keep the magic of miracles alive in our lives...

There are iconic lines from famous series which make their way into humdrum conversations.
One of the most famous ones from the Bard of Avon(William Shakespeare) in his famous play, ’Hamlet’, “To be or not to be, that is the question.”
I was telling a colleague about how I preferred getting my prized Littmann stethoscope repaired, instead of replaced, as I have bonded with it.
Out of the blue, another  proclaimed, “ Coz it’s the stethoscope which chooses the doctor, not vice versa.” I could hear Mr Ollivander from the Harry Potter book declaiming the same line about a wand & its wizard.
Gobsmacked I asked him if he was a Potter fan. “Of course!”
When I saw a chocolate éclair for the first time, my heart travelled to those lazy summer days of school vacations, the dog-eared yellow pages of Enid Blyton & Fatty(no body shaming intended, just a pet-name ), eating them with the Find-Outers.
When I described a back stabbing friend, my brother’s comeback was, ”You too Brutus.”(from Julius Caeser, Shakespeare)
Of course, the tweens now have cults for Jameson- Grayson from Inheritance games or the SoKeefe/Fitzphie  from Keepers series. They argue vociferously about their favourite.
You realise that though times change, children find ways to express their love, when your little one fixes a sticker saying, ‘Always’ on your phone case(denoting eternal love from Harry Potter).

Cough…cough…khong…khong…
The clinic sounds like a symphony since the beginning of 2026.1.23children of all age groups, many a times with their parents also, all coughing in different tones & rhythms.
The cacophony reminds one of an orchestra with different instruments being played as per the age.
Should I give preference to the inspiratory stridor of bronchiolitis?
Or should I first look at the child who is wheezing?
What about the mother who has dark circles under her eyes because her infant kept her up all night with a congested nose?
And then there are the high grade fevers who aren’t responding to anti-pyretics…what if one gets a febrile seizure? 
The clinic staff is literally at the wits end trying to triage patients & their parents on the basis of their severity.
So why such a spate of respiratory illnesses requiring doctor visits when we could have been flying kites in this season.
Reasons:-
1)Exceptionally cold weather triggering bronchospasm & viral infections in susceptible population.
2)Non-indigenous(vacation infections) to the non-immune population.
3)Enclosed places without ventilation leading to contracting infections easily.
4)Construction debris without proper precautions.
5)Vehicular pollution.
The last two factors have caused a smog to rival our capital. It contains irritants which are triggering cough, especially for people who are up in the morning like school children or people who go for morning walks in polluted areas.
Possible solutions :- next blog.

Calling a national level Paralympic winner as a chief guest, starts the day  on a brave note…a note which heralds the indomitable spirit of human beings to fight against insurmountable odds…true spirit of sports!There is something incredibly thrilling about sports day:-the nip in the air, the crisply ironed uniforms, the polished shoes,the chalk-marked tracks,the flattened ground,the array of medals!The dhum-dhum,military like precision of the march past with the house captains holding their respective flags high;the left-right-left compelling all parents to reminisce their own simpler era, when cheering did not involve cheerleaders, just screaming your lungs out.

Torch bearing à la the Olympics, you literally pass the torch once you are tired, coz the light goes on eternally.

A child who falls while performing gymnastics,but succeeds on her partners encouragement…the sheer joy on their faces on turning their failure into success…

‘Trophies gather dust, but memories last forever.’

A sprint which seems like a foregone conclusion, when winner gives it another turn, by suddenly galloping the last few meters in the sheer excitement of being the sure winner.

The true sportsman who cinches the runner-up in a bear hug at the finishing line and both jump for joy while continuing to hug.

Sports, whether individual or team require a multitude of people who contribute to victory…

Sports teaches us,

‘Alone, we CAN;but together, we WILL.’
